checkpoints: On each download-dialog preparation check, interpret the resolved service value using PREPARATION_STATUS: false is pending and true is ready.
After a pending result for the current dialog generation, arrange another preparation check through the public retry scheduler and expose retryScheduled consistently.
Before applying an asynchronous result or scheduling its continuation, verify that the dialog instance is not disposed and that the request still belongs to the current generation.
On a ready result for the current generation, stop loading, avoid further retries, and record the request token as completed at most once.
On close, reopen, restart, or unmount, retain the existing generation and retry cleanup semantics so stale callbacks cannot mutate the current dialog lifecycle.
forbidden_effects: Do not mark a token completed or otherwise deliver it while the service reports PREPARATION_STATUS.PENDING.
Do not allow a pending result from an invalidated generation to schedule or perform another check.
Do not allow an already scheduled retry from an invalidated generation to operate on a reopened dialog or a replacement token.
Do not publish state after the hook has been disposed.
Do not change BackgroundExportPanel/useBackgroundPreparation semantics: closing that panel must continue not to cancel workspace-owned work.
Do not alter tests, configuration, the public preparation service status meanings, or scheduler interfaces.
lifecycle_identity: A download-dialog polling lifecycle is identified by the hook instance and lifecycle.current.generation.
The token captured when a check begins is the identity used when recording successful completion.
start() creates a new generation for the current token; reopen(nextToken) changes the token and creates a new generation; close() invalidates the current generation when invalidateOnClose is true.
Unmount sets disposed and begins a new generation, invalidating asynchronous results and retry callbacks belonging to the mounted lifecycle.

obligations.text: The file download dialog must continue checking when checkPreparation resolves to PREPARATION_STATUS.PENDING.
The file download dialog must record completion—and thereby make the file eligible for delivery—only after checkPreparation resolves to PREPARATION_STATUS.READY for the current lifecycle generation.
Pending checks must use schedulePreparationRetry for continuation, and any retained retry handle must be canceled and cleared when the generation is invalidated or the hook is disposed.
Asynchronous service results and scheduled retry callbacks must be generation-safe so close, reopen, restart, and unmount cannot let stale work affect the active dialog or replacement token.

Existing download-dialog observables must remain coherent: visible, loading, retryScheduled, checkCount, token, and completed snapshots must reflect the active polling lifecycle, with completed tokens remaining unique.
Background export polling behavior is outside the requested change and must be preserved, including continued workspace-owned work after its progress panel is closed.

ordering_barriers: A pending result must be received and validated against disposed/generation state before a retry is scheduled.
A retry callback must clear its retained handle and retryScheduled indication before beginning the next check.
A ready result must be validated against disposed/generation state before loading is cleared or the captured token is added to completed.
Generation invalidation must cancel and clear an existing scheduled retry before stale work can continue.
File completion/delivery must occur after, never before, a ready status.
preservation: Preserve DownloadDialog's use of usePreparation(token, { invalidateOnClose: true }).
Preserve start() making the dialog visible and beginning a fresh generation for the current token.
Preserve close() hiding the dialog and, for DownloadDialog, invalidating the active generation.
Preserve reopen(nextToken) updating the token, showing the dialog, and checking within a fresh generation.
Preserve snapshot copying completed rather than exposing the mutable internal array.
Preserve checkCount incrementing once for each actual service check.
Preserve useBackgroundPreparation's existing pending retry loop and its explicit background-work ownership across close.
Preserve the preparation API meanings false/PENDING and true/READY and its installed transport/scheduler boundaries.
scope: Business-code change is limited to the file download dialog preparation behavior implemented by src/DownloadDialog.jsx and src/usePreparation.js, using src/preparation-api.js.
src/useBackgroundPreparation.js and src/BackgroundExportPanel.jsx are preservation references, not targets for changing download-dialog ownership semantics.
The required behavior covers pending-to-ready polling, completion/delivery gating, retry cleanup, and dialog lifecycle invalidation.

supporting_evidence.quote: The preparation service can now report that a file is still pending before it becomes ready.
Update the file download dialog so it keeps checking pending preparation and delivers the file only after a ready status.
// transport resolves false while preparation is pending and true when ready.
// Closing this progress panel does not cancel workspace-owned work.

triggers: Calling start() on the download dialog begins checking the current token in a fresh generation.
Calling reopen(nextToken) begins checking nextToken in a fresh generation.
A current-generation PREPARATION_STATUS.PENDING result triggers scheduling of another check.
Execution of the scheduled retry callback triggers the next service check.
A current-generation PREPARATION_STATUS.READY result triggers completion recording and ends polling for that run.
Calling close() on DownloadDialog or unmounting the hook invalidates active dialog work and clears scheduled retry state.
unknowns: The public task and sources do not define retry delay, backoff, maximum attempts, or timeout; those remain delegated to schedulePreparationRetry.
The public sources do not show a separate file-delivery callback or download API; the only observable readiness/delivery marker supplied here is the completed token list.
The public sources do not define rejection/error handling for checkPreparation or scheduler failures.

The public sources do not specify whether repeated start() calls for an already completed token should skip checking; existing behavior starts a fresh check and should not be weakened without further evidence.
The public sources do not define whether token prop changes without reopen(nextToken) must automatically begin a new preparation lifecycle.
